# Let me continue clicking middle red to complete the cycle and see the full pattern
# Also track the full state to understand the goal

ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')

def get_state_snapshot(ascii_lines):
    cells = []
    for r in range(15, 50):
        for c in range(10, 55):
            ch = ascii_lines[r][c]
            if ch not in ('c', 'G', 'g', 'w', 'B', 'R', 'N'):
                cells.append((r, c, ch))
    return tuple(sorted(cells))

# Click middle red 4 more times to complete the cycle (should wrap back to 29-30)
for i in range(4):
    before = get_state_snapshot(current_frame.ascii.split('\n'))
    result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 26, 'col': 14}])
    after = get_state_snapshot(current_frame.ascii.split('\n'))
    
    before_set = set(before)
    after_set = set(after)
    changed = []
    for (r, c, new_ch) in after_set - before_set:
        for (r2, c2, old_ch) in before_set:
            if r == r2 and c == c2:
                changed.append((r, c, old_ch, new_ch))
                break
    
    cols = sorted(set(c for _, c, _, _ in changed))
    rows = sorted(set(r for r, _, _, _ in changed))
    print(f"Click {i+8}: rows={rows}, cols={cols}, changes: {[(c, old, new) for _, c, old, new in changed[:2]]}")
    
    if last_action_result.get('level_completed'):
        print("LEVEL COMPLETED!")
        break

# Now let's get a full snapshot of the current state
print("\n--- Current non-background cells ---")
cells = get_state_snapshot(current_frame.ascii.split('\n'))
for r, c, ch in cells:
    print(f"  ({r},{c}): {ch}")
